lessons: Don't assert 'no rebase in progress' after drain(). By then runner cleanup has run worktree remove --force and prune, which deletes .git/worktrees/<stem>, so the check passes even when a rebase was left behind. Observe the worktree at the moment of refusal instead.

In eval/shakeout/merge.py only, wrap the bench's Git worktree_remove (or the equivalent seam) for this stem. Before it delegates, run git status and git rev-parse --git-dir in the worktree, then record the rebase state, the worktree HEAD and main's HEAD.

After drain(), assert on the recorded snapshot: neither rebase-merge nor rebase-apply exists under the git-dir, git status shows no rebase, worktree HEAD == review.reviewed_sha, and main HEAD == its pre-admission SHA.

Prove the check can fail: temporarily stub Git.rebase so it skips the abort, confirm the member goes red, then remove the stub. Make no edits to chupa/git.py or runner.py, which are outside the fence.
